claims.claim: Hospitality centers on the host-guest relationship; the English words host, guest, hotel, hostel, and hospital descend from the Latin hospes ('guest, host, stranger') and an older Indo-European root for a reciprocal guest-host bond.
Hospitality can be defined as the business of helping people feel welcome and relaxed and to enjoy themselves, centered on providing lodging, food and drink, and welcome to people away from home.
The hospitality industry is essentially the combination of the accommodation and food-and-beverage sectors, which together form the largest segment of the broader tourism industry.
Tourism-related activity is commonly grouped, via NAICS, into five sectors: accommodation, food and beverage, recreation and entertainment, transportation, and travel services.

Hospitality is a service field whose offerings are intangible, perishable, and inseparable (produced and consumed at the same time, usually in the presence of the provider); an unsold hotel night or airline seat is lost revenue once the time passes.

UN Tourism (UNWTO) defines tourism as the movement of people to places outside their usual environment for less than a year for business, leisure, or other personal purposes; hospitality and tourism overlap but are distinct, since hospitality also serves local, non-traveling guests.

The Tremont House, which opened in Boston in 1829, is widely regarded as the first modern first-class hotel, introducing private locked guest rooms, indoor plumbing and running water, a reception area, bellboys, and free soap.

Ellsworth Statler's first permanent hotel, built in Buffalo in 1907, was among the first major hotels to include a private bath and running water in every room, advancing the standardized modern hotel and chain model.
The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics groups much of the field in its Leisure and Hospitality supersector, which combines Arts, Entertainment, and Recreation with Accommodation and Food Services.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether the Tremont House is 'the first modern hotel' is a popular characterization rather than an undisputed technical fact.
positions: Widely cited (Wikipedia, popular histories) as the first modern first-class hotel in the United States for its cluster of innovations.
Other establishments and earlier inns also claim precedence for individual features.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson uses the hedged phrasing 'widely regarded as the first modern first-class hotel' and treats it as illustrative of an evolution rather than an exact record.
